questions.title: Differentiate an exponential model
questions.prompt_html:
Consider the function \(y=- 4 e^{x - 2} - 4\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).
questions.solution_html:
The derivative of the exponent \(x - 2\) is \(1\), so the exponential term contributes \(- 4 e^{x - 2}\) while the constant term differentiates to zero.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=- \frac{4 e^{x}}{e^{2}}\).

questions.title: Differentiate a trigonometric function in radians
questions.prompt_html:
The curve is \(y=\cos{\left(3 x + \frac{\pi}{4} \right)} - 2\). Angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

    [2]

  2. Find the exact gradient when \(x=- \frac{\pi}{36}\).

    [2]

  3. Evaluate \(\frac{\mathrm d^2y}{\mathrm dx^2}\) when \(x=- \frac{\pi}{36}\).

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Let \(u=3 x + \frac{\pi}{4}\), so \(u^\prime=3\). For angles in radians, cosine becomes negative sine. Multiply the outer derivative by \(3\).

At the stated input in the later parts, the full angle in the formula will be \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=- 3 \sin{\left(3 x + \frac{\pi}{4} \right)}\).

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=- 3 \sin{\left(3 x + \frac{\pi}{4} \right)}\).

At \(x=- \frac{\pi}{36}\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(- \frac{3}{2}\).

Answer: \(- \frac{3}{2}\).

(c)

Differentiate the gradient function again to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm d^2y}{\mathrm dx^2}=- 9 \cos{\left(3 x + \frac{\pi}{4} \right)}\).

The inner angle is \(3 (- \frac{\pi}{36}) + \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{6}\). Evaluate at this radian angle.

Answer: \(- \frac{9 \sqrt{3}}{2}\).

questions.title: Find a turn of a trigonometric curve on a restricted interval
questions.prompt_html:
The curve is \(y=\sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} + \cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 2\) where \(- \frac{\pi}{6}<x<\frac{5 \pi}{6}\). Angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

    [2]

  2. Find the exact x-coordinate of the stationary point.

    [2]

  3. Give the y-coordinate and justify the type of stationary point.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The derivative of \(\sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\) is \(\cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\), and the derivative of \(\cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\) is \(- \sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\).

Multiply both contributions by \(1\); the constant differentiates to zero.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=- \sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} + \cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\).

(b)

At a stationary point, \(\cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}=\sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\). The original x-interval makes the full angle lie between \(0\) and \(\pi\).

The equal sine and cosine occur at full angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) in this interval. Solve \(x + \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{4}\) for x.

Answer: \(\frac{\pi}{12}\).

(c)

Evaluate the original formula at the full angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) to obtain \(y=-2 + \sqrt{2}\).

The second derivative \(- \sin{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - \cos{\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\) gives \(- \sqrt{2}\) at this input, so the point is a local maximum.
questions.hint_html: Convert the interval for x into an interval for the full radian angle before choosing the root.

marking_criteria.description_html: Differentiate both trigonometric terms and include the chain factor.
Solve for the full angle in the stated interval, then isolate x.
Justify the local maximum by a valid derivative test.
